card.name: Citation and science-article scaffolding
card.fires_on: Small structural spots in science writing outside clinical text: attribution verbs after a quote, author surnames in reference lists, and digits inside numbers or ranges.

modes.label: Quote attribution
modes.description: A speech verb such as says or said right after a quoted sentence in a research news story.
modes.example: under a wider variety of conditions,"<< says>> Williams.

modes.label: Reference list pieces
modes.description: Author surnames or punctuation inside a citation list.
modes.example: Clesceri, L.S., Green<<berg>>, A.E., and Trussell

modes.label: Digits in numbers
modes.description: A single digit inside a year, DOI or numeric range.

card.writes: Little clear effect; it pushes up DNA-type words and lowers patient and clinical words, steering away from clinical text.
card.plain: It fires on scaffolding in non-clinical science writing, such as quote attributions, citation names and digits in numbers.
